title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 208 (Report on inspection made)

content.overview: Section 208 requires the Registrar or inspector to submit a report in writing to the Central Government after an inspection or inquiry under section 206. The report may recommend further investigation. It is not itself an adjudication. Action on the report may include ordering investigation under section 210 or assigning the case to the Serious Fraud Investigation Office under section 212.
content.glance: After s. 206 inspection/inquiry: Registrar or inspector submits written report to Central Government; may recommend further investigation; not an adjudication; may lead to s. 210 investigation or s. 212 SFIO assignment.
content.study: The Registrar or inspector shall, after the inspection of the books of account or an inquiry under section 206 and other books and papers of the company under section 206, submit a report in writing to the Central Government along with such documents, if any, and such report may, if necessary, include a recommendation that further investigation into the affairs of the company is necessary giving his reasons in support. Current-law framing: confirm completion of s. 206 inspection or inquiry; ensure written report to Central Government; note any recommendation for further investigation; distinguish the report from adjudication and from the investigation powers under ss. 210 and 212.

sections.heading: Trigger
sections.body: Report follows inspection of books or inquiry under section 206.

sections.heading: Form and Addressee
sections.body: Written report to the Central Government, with such documents as may be attached.

sections.heading: Recommendation
sections.body: Report may recommend further investigation into the affairs of the company, with reasons in support.

sections.heading: Consequence
sections.body: Not an adjudication; may lead to investigation under s. 210 or SFIO assignment under s. 212.

examples.title: Recommendation for investigation
examples.body: After a s. 206 inquiry, the Registrar submits a written report to the Central Government recommending further investigation because the affairs appear to be conducted in a manner prejudicial to members. Section 208 expressly allows such a recommendation with reasons.

examples.title: Report is not a conviction
examples.body: A director argues that the s. 208 report itself finds him guilty. The report is a communication to the Central Government; it is not an adjudication of guilt.

hypotheticals.question: Does a s. 208 report automatically open an SFIO investigation?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The report may recommend further investigation. Whether the Central Government orders investigation under s. 210 or assigns the case to SFIO under s. 212 is a separate decision.

distinctions.title: Report on inspection (s. 208) vs power to inspect/inquire (s. 206)
distinctions.left: Written report to Central Government after inspection/inquiry
distinctions.right: Registrar’s power to call for information, inspect and inquire

misconceptions.trap: The inspection report under s. 208 is a binding finding against the company.
misconceptions.correction: Section 208 requires a written report to the Central Government. It may recommend further investigation but is not itself an adjudication.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 208 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm s. 206 inspection/inquiry completed. II. Check written report to CG. III. Note any recommendation. IV. Distinguish investigation steps. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Inspection facts; report status; recommendation; precise relief.

enhancement.legalPrinciple: Inspection outcomes are channelled to the Central Government through a formal written report before investigation powers are engaged.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 208 closes the inspection loop by reporting to the Central Government.
